items.title: Novelty
items.summary: An essay on why visual novelty in UI loses its punch the more it appears — and why the sharpest designers treat surprise as a scarce resource, reserved for the moments that earn it.
items.why: Maps directly onto Cuemath's gamification design: knowing when a belt-level celebration or XP animation actually lands versus when it becomes noise is exactly the 90%/10% question Rauno is answering.

items.title: Cognitive Load Is a Budget, Not an Enemy: Design for the Brain's 4 Chunks
items.summary: A research-backed guide that reframes cognitive load — the mental effort an interface demands from users — as a four-slot working memory budget to spend deliberately, with 26 concrete design guidelines across perception, understanding, decision-making, and action.
items.why: In math education, the subject itself carries high intrinsic load; every Cuemath screen that adds extraneous interface friction steals from the budget kids need to understand the math. These guidelines translate directly to the practice app.

items.title: Charlotte Rohde's new typeface has heart-dotted i's and a plan to overwrite problematic men
items.summary: Berlin designer Charlotte Rohde created Oficía Mono, a monospace typeface with heart-dotted i's that doubles as the protagonist of her sci-fi feminist novel — built as a deliberate reworking of Gill Sans and its problematic creator.
items.why: A typeface built around a complete conceptual premise rather than just craft decisions — a useful model for how Cuemath's editorial type choices could carry a point of view about who the brand is and who it speaks to.

items.title: Enacting Constructive Conflicts with AI Agents to Enhance Reconsideration among Novice Interaction Designers
items.summary: A Carnegie Mellon study found that an AI agent that argues against a designer's choices — rather than offering praise — prompted participants to reconsider and substantially improve their work, generating more iterations than self-reflection or written guidance alone.
items.why: Points at how AI could be used in Cuemath's design process not just as a generative tool but as a structured critic — building in the adversarial pushback that usually only comes from a senior review or a difficult stakeholder.

items.title: The Antithesis Principle
items.summary: Shreyas Doshi's framework for turning a behavioral observation inside out: smart people apply an insight to influence others; wise people apply the opposite inward, to eliminate the same tendency from their own thinking.
items.why: Sharp frame for someone who designs external motivation systems — building products that exploit how users' brains seek validation while personally cultivating the intrinsic drive that makes design work good.
